TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
WEDNESDAY, 1 FEBRUARY 2023 AT 10:02 AM (AEST)
DAY 29
MR JUSTIN GREGGERY KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MS RENEE BERRY, Counsel Assisting
MS DOMINIQUE HOGAN-DORAN SC, for the Commonwealth
MR TRENT GLOVER, for the Commonwealth
MR MIN GUO, for Ms Rachelle Miller
MR PHILIP SOLOMON KC, for The Hon Alan Tudge

COMMISSIONER: Can I have the appearances, please?
MR GREGGERY: Yes. If it please the Commission, today I appear with Ms Berry.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you.
MS HOGAN-DORAN: May it please the Commission, today I appear with Mr Glover for the
Commonwealth.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you.
MR SOLOMON: May it please the Commission, my name is Solomon. I'm appearing for
Mr Tudge.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. And Mr Guo?
MR GUO: And, yes, if the Commission pleases, I appear for Ms Miller.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. That's all? Thanks. Mr Greggery, you're calling Mr Tudge?
MR GREGGERY: I am, yes. The witness for today is the Honourable Alan Tudge MP.
COMMISSIONER: Mr Tudge, will you take an oath or an affirmation?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: An oath.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. Could you stand and that will be administered.
<ALAN EDWARD TUDGE, SWORN
<EXAMINATION BY MR GREGGERY KC
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Take a seat. Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Thank you, Commissioner. Can you tell the Commission your full name,
please, Mr Tudge?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Alan Edward Tudge.
MR GREGGERY: Mr Tudge, were you served with a Notice to Give a Statement and Produce
Documents -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, I was.
MR GREGGERY: - dated, I think, 17 October 2022?

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I believe that was the date.
MR GREGGERY: And have you prepared a Statement for the Commission in response to that
notice dated 20 January 2023?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Mr Tudge, I see you have a paper copy of it there before you. Can I take you
to page 57. There's no need to bring this up on the screen. At the bottom of page 57, the last
two lines commence, "I do not recall.” You can see that?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: I understand you wish to withdraw that sentence - or those two sentences
from your Statement?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Correct.
MR GREGGERY: Commissioner -
COMMISSIONER: "I do not recall the other cases" - from there on?
MR GREGGERY: That's right, yes.
COMMISSIONER: That's coming out, is it?
MR GREGGERY: Yes. At the bottom of page 58. That's a withdrawal that I accept, and it will
be removed from the Statement which is tendered online.
COMMISSIONER: Mr Guo, that was the basis of your leave, I think.
MR GUO: It was.
COMMISSIONER: Alright. Well, I will withdraw the leave, then. Obviously if something pops
up and you want to make an instanter application you can, but for the present you don't
have leave to cross-examine.
MR GUO: If the Commission pleases.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. I'm told it was only the second sentence, not the first, in that -
COMMISSIONER: Okay. I don't think it's too critical.
MR GREGGERY: Mr Tudge, is your Statement, with that redaction, true and correct to the

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Commissioner, it is convenient at this point to tender the exhibits for the
day. There is a draft exhibit list listing Exhibits 4621 to 4823. The document that was shown
to Mr Jongen yesterday, which related to the radio transcript of an interview he participated
in, I also tender. It will become 4824 on the updated list.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. That was an ABC 24 transcript.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
COMMISSIONER: I forgot myself that it hadn't been tendered. Mr Solomon, I have just
noticed that somebody has given me a witness and counsel list, and you've got juniors
according to it. Is that not right?
MR SOLOMON: Mr Jeffreys is in Brisbane. He is attending to some other matters this
morning. He may attend this afternoon, but he may not. And so I didn't want to announce his
appearance and find he wasn't here.
COMMISSIONER: Fair enough. Okay. You know your own business. Thank you.
MR SOLOMON: Thank you.
COMMISSIONER: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. Mr Tudge, as you say at paragraph 3 of your Statement, you were
the Human Services Minister from 18 February 2016 until 20 December 2017; that's correct?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And during that period of time as Minister for the Department of Human
Services, you oversaw the administration of various policies, in a service delivery sense, by
the Department?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: The question meaning is that correct? Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And one of those came to be known as the Robodebt Scheme, which
attracted significant media and political attention during your period as Minister?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: The OCI became - the Online Compliance Intervention became to be
coined by the Labor Party as the Robodebt Scheme, yes.
MR GREGGERY: One of the early Briefings that you received after you commenced as
Minister on 18 February 2016 was a Briefing provided to you on 23 February 2016. There are
three volumes of folders before you, and they contain the documents that I will take you to

throughout the day. So if you wish to refer to the hard copy document, I can take you to a
tab number.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: That would be good, please.
MR GREGGERY: Tab 1 in volume 1 is Exhibit 4621, CTH.2009.0006.2319.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Mmm.
MS HOGAN-DORAN: On the exhibit list, that document is marked as 4623. I will just check if
your tab numbers are out, or you have misspoken?
MR GREGGERY: No, that's correct. There is an error in the tab number. It is behind tab 1 in
the bundle, I think. You found it behind tab 1, Mr Tudge?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't know what I'm looking for now, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Do you see the tab numbers down the right-hand side?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, I'm at tab 1.
MR GREGGERY: And is that the Ministerial Brief - sorry, Department of Human Services
Executive Minute?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes. Received on the 23rd of Feb 2016?
MR GREGGERY: That's it.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. It is Exhibit 4623. The document is signed by you on 3 March
2016?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I presume so. It's been redacted, as you can see.
MR GREGGERY: The signature has been redacted, but the note appears beside your title. The
purpose of a Briefing such as this is to bring you, as the new Minister, up to speed with the
topic - or the contents of what's contained in the Executive Minute?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Well, yes, I mean, it's to inform me. It says to note the information
provided in this document, so that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: The relevance of the document for today's proceedings deals with the
question of the overpayment of social security benefits to various recipients and the Budget
Measures which were then in existence to address that question of overpayments. Do you
see?

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: That looks to be the case.
MR GREGGERY: And we can go to page 2 of the document, ending .2320 in the top right
corner. You will see the subheading 'Current Budget Measures and Future Savings
Possibilities'.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Paragraphs 9 and 10 deal with the Strengthening the Integrity of Welfare
Payments package of measures which was announced in the previous Budget. Do you see
that?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, I can see that.
MR GREGGERY: And it was identified for you, by way of information, that the savings set out
in paragraph 9 flow from one of the eight initiatives which involved data matching PAYG
income declared to the Department with PAYG income declared to the Australian Taxation
Office.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: In paragraph 10?
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Do you see that?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: The point is, Mr Tudge, you were informed at a very early time of the
significance of the particular measure to the Government's Budget?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I was certainly informed of the Budget Measures, and I was aware of
the Budget Measures from 2015, and that is a summary of one of them in paragraph 10.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And it confirmed to you that this particular measure, which became
known to you subsequently as the Manual PAYG Measure, involved a significant number of
interventions during the '15/16 financial year and an even greater number of online
interventions during the '16/17 financial year?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: That's right.
MR GREGGERY: The information in paragraph 10 identified a significant business process
redesign, which enabled the increase in interventions from approximately 20,000 annually to
400,000 annually in the '16/17 financial year?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Mmm.
MR GREGGERY: And would that be the first occasion when you gained a degree of familiarity
with, or understanding of, the PAYG measure which was conducted while you were Minister?

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: To - to my - to my recollection, and certainly having at least scanned
the 8000-odd documents which you provided to me, I don't believe there was any document
before this time. It was the incoming Minister's Brief, which of course is an important
document, which outlines what the priorities are for the government in that. And that
included a specific Briefing on welfare integrity. And in that Briefing, it didn't specifically, to
my recollection, go to this level of detail.
MR GREGGERY: Can I take you to tab 3, ATO.0001.695.6261, Exhibit 4625. This is an email
between persons within the Taxation Office the following day, that is, the day after you
received the Minister's Executive Minute -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Mmm.
MR GREGGERY: - which purports to attribute a position to you in these terms, by reference
to a Mr Lumley at DHS, in the context of a meeting which was said to take place the following
day. It is said of you that you were:
...excited by the outcome of the moneys recovered as part the recent data-matching
activities.
If I pause there, do you recall taking that view or holding that position?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't.
MR GREGGERY: Right. The concern that was communicated was that you may want even
more historical data, that is, as far back as 2000, to recover even more overpayments. Do
you recall expressing anything along those lines to persons in DHS within that first week?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't. I would say that this is within five weeks of me becoming
Minister.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, that's right. Certainly it was a significant aspect of - that is, this measure,
the PAYG measure, was important to the government's approach to a balanced Budget?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Sorry, say that question again?
MR GREGGERY: The PAYG measure about which you received the specific Briefing the day
before, was important to the government's approach to a balanced Budget?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't know if I had that knowledge at the time. I wasn't a member
of Cabinet and so wasn't part of the Cabinet decision in what was April of 2015 to determine
that measure and the purpose of that measure at that time. I - sorry, go on.
MR GREGGERY: That's alright. I didn't mean to cut you off, if you had finished. Did you
understand, though, from your role as a Minister that the government was striving for a
balanced Budget?

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Of course.
MR GREGGERY: And this -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I think the public understood that.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And this measure -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: That was a good ambition, as it always should be.
MR GREGGERY: This measure represented a significant aspect of savings available for
Forward Estimates, to your understanding?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: It's - in the context of the Social Services Budget, which was at the
time, I believe, 160 or 170 billion dollars, it's - what was the amount again? It was - in the
first document, I think it referred to the amount. So 900 - 800 million?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: So maybe .5 per cent of the Social Security Budget. So it's not
insignificant, but it's not -
MR GREGGERY: In relative terms to the Social Security Budget it might not have been
significant, but it was, so far as a balanced Budget concerned, a significant savings measure?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: It's still significant.
MR GREGGERY: Did you ever consider, as the note suggests, whether the PAYG measure
could be extended to increase the prospect of savings for the Department?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I - I considered it, as I outlined in my Statement, when at one stage
the Finance Minister, Mathias - who was Mathias Cormann at the time - approached me and
asked if there were further opportunities within welfare compliance for financial savings.
And obviously the Finance Minister is a very senior Minister. I was a junior Minister at the
time. And as I outline in my Statement - and I can refer to the paragraphs if it's useful,
Mr Greggery - that I had asked my Secretary that question, and my Secretary subsequently
provided some advice in relation to that, which I, from memory, communicated back to the
Finance Minister. And, indeed, that was - subsequently became the subject of New Policy
Proposals.
MR GREGGERY: More specifically, did you consider whether the data-matching activities
which founded the PAYG measure were able to be extended to earlier years, that is, earlier
than the -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: No, I - I don't at all recall that. So that's why, going back to the email,
which you've got up on the screen, I simply don't recall that. Now, the email I point out,

but he's from the Taxation Office. So I never would have - I don't know that name. I never
would have dealt with that person's name. Judging by his title, which I think is clear on the
screen, he's not a senior person within the Australian Taxation Office, a relatively junior
person within the Australian Taxation Office, reporting presumably to two other people here
from the Taxation Office as well, names again I'm not familiar with and presumably still
relatively junior, and they've had a phone call from Ben Lumley - sorry, I didn't mean to - that
name is mentioned - at DHS, a name that again I'm not familiar with at DHS, and he's
referring to a conversation which he had with DHS executives who apparently had a meeting
with me previously and a further meeting with me tomorrow. So in that context and with
my - with no memory of suggesting at that very early stage to say, "We should be going back
further years," I just simply don't recall that.
MR GREGGERY: That's right. I think as I indicated, it was not an email to which you were a
party, but it attributed a position to you potentially, and I'm just -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: It did, and I'm simply pointing out it is an attribution going through
the chain of many people from a junior level - from a senior level referring down to a junior
level in a different Department and then across to a senior level, presumably again in a
separate Department. That's all I'm pointing out.
MR GREGGERY: Can I take you to tab 4 in the bundle, Exhibit 4626, RBD.9999.0001.0372_R.
This was a joint media release from you and the Minister for Social Services, the Honourable
Christian Porter, 2 March 2016, which referred to, broadly, the topic contained in the title of
ensuring welfare integrity and specifically two bills being introduced to the Parliament on
that date to strengthen the integrity of the welfare system. One of those related to the
removal of the six-year limit on debt recovery. That appears to be within a relatively short
space of time following the previous email on 24 February to which you were not a party. In
the context of that joint media release, are you able to say anything more from your memory
about whether you considered going - extending the measure to earlier financial years?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Again, if I look at this press release, Mr Greggery, this is in relation to
introducing legislation. I mean, as you would be aware, the legislative process is a lengthy
one. You don't make a decision today and introduce legislation tomorrow. So I would be very
certain that this would have gone through a Cabinet process before I was even in the
Ministry, and with those decisions made probably in 2015 and then the bills would have
been drafted and then scheduled to be introduced, obviously, on the 2nd of March. So this
press release would have been announcing simply the introduction of what would have
been, effectively, Christian Porter's bills he had responsibility for - the Social Security Act,
which I assume was the Act which was being amended here. And it's - this press release, I
think, is no more than summarising what the two bills do.
MR GREGGERY: I'm not suggesting you were involved in any of the decision-making which
led to the legislative process described in the bill but simply that it appears that you had
knowledge that the six-year time limit on debt recovery was being removed by legislative
process at this point in time, and in that context, with that knowledge, whether you
considered that within your Department the measure might be able to be extended to

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I - I don't recall - I don't recall considering going back earlier
than - because this was in 2016, going back earlier than 2010. And my recollection is that we
didn't go back earlier than 2010. I think 2010-11, we might have gone back to that financial
year, is my recollection. But I don't recall that we ever went back further than that.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: And I - and, yes, I will just leave it there.
MR GREGGERY: If you could go to tab 5, please, Exhibit 4627, CTH.3061.0005.3150.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Sorry, tab 5?
MR GREGGERY: Tab 5, yes. Again, this is an email which you are not a party, but it attributes
a position to you.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Mmm.
MR GREGGERY: It says that your position was that you were keen to announce the
Strengthening the Integrity of Welfare Payments measure had achieved the first year's
saving expectations already, and you were keen for an announcement about that. Do you
remember being keen, as the email says, to promote the measures undertaken by the
Department, particularly this one?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't recall this in particular, but it doesn't surprise me that if it's a
measure of the government's that you're hitting a milestone, that you might want to
announce the milestone.
MR GREGGERY: Announcing that you might have hit a milestone earlier - or the Department,
of which you were the Minister, hit a milestone early reflected well on you?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Like, as a Minister, you're - you're obviously promoting the
government's agenda as a Minister. These were - the decisions for all of these were made
before I became Minister. I had only become Minister by that stage - what day did I become
Minister again? 18th of February. So you're talking about a couple of weeks afterwards. And
so it was an opportunity to say that this measure was started nine months earlier, eight
months before I became Minister, was underway and being implemented and apparently on
track.
MR GREGGERY: Or even ahead of schedule.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: And if it's a - even - even ahead of schedule. But certainly meeting
the - the milestone, which was announced.
MR GREGGERY: And to your mind, that was worthy of, as you'll see in the next two tabs, a

achievement of the measures that the government had implemented before you became the
Minister?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Well, yes, I think we did put out a - I don't know if we did put out a
media release on that. We did. I can see it now on tab 7.
MR GREGGERY: But is it - what I'm suggesting to you, Mr Tudge - and we can go to tab 7,
Exhibit 4629 -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I don't have the second page of that. I've just got the first page.
MR GREGGERY: I've only got one page as well. But it indicates media contact at the bottom,
which would generally be the conclusion of it, I think. The media release under your name,
the day after that email was sent, 11 March 2016, confirms effectively a media announcable.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: It might be described that the welfare compliance measures were ahead of
schedule.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Sorry, the - you asked me to confirm that there - yes, the heading
says, 'Welfare Compliance Measure Ahead of Schedule'. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And the - behind tab 6 is a media article from The Herald Sun, Exhibit 4628,
CTH.3000.0012.7824, which - perhaps if we just go to the second page. Thank you. Various
statements in the short article are attributed to you. You would agree with me they are
statements which paint the government's agenda in a positive light and reflect well on you
also?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: The overall - I mean, I assume that those quotes are taken from the
media release, which - we don't have page 2 of the media release. If we -
MR GREGGERY: I think -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I assume those quotes are accurately taken from my media release,
which I would have - I would have approved those statements.
MR GREGGERY: Commissioner, I can indicate the document produced to the Commission
contains only a single page, which is the exhibit. Mr Tudge, are you familiar with the process
in your capacity as Minister for the Department of Human Services of providing a media
release in advance to a journalist, together with some lines which have been approved by
you, and maybe some additional information for a journalist to be able to run a story?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I think every single Minister uses that process.
MR GREGGERY: I'm not suggesting -

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Sorry. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: - there's anything improper about it.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: That's okay. And it may be that that process explains why, although there are
not specific lines attributed to you in the media release, the journalist may still have been
able to have recourse to a document which did indicate statements attributed to you which
had been cleared by you, according to that process?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Typically, if the journalist was quoting me, I would typically want to
see from my office every quote that was attributed to me before it went to a journalist.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And speaking broadly -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, I don't know if this was directly given to this particular journalist
in advance as an exclusive. Typically, if it was, it would say "exclusive" on the article, which it
doesn't say. So I don't know whether that's how it was done on this occasion. It actually
appears that it wasn't, that it's more that this journalist has picked up the media release.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Speaking generally about the attention to detail you paid in respect
of media relating to the Department and to your office, would you accept that you paid a
very high level of attention to the detail of the media generated in respect of your
Department?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: So the question was, did I pay a lot of detail to the media in relation
to my Department?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: You do pay attention broadly to the media as a Minister. You can't
be across everything if there's a lot of media. And with many, many outlets across the
country, many online outlets, many blogs, et cetera, you just simply can't be across
absolutely everything. So you do rely upon your team in your office to assist you in alerting
you to significant media stories as well.
MR GREGGERY: Two aspects of your reliance on systems within your office or within the
Department were, firstly, that you had a media adviser, just as every Minister does, who had
responsibility for drawing to your attention media of direct relevance to your role; that's
correct? And that was done on a daily basis?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Typically, yes.
MR GREGGERY: And you also had access to, or were the recipient of, daily, sometimes
multiple times a day, emails from the Department which circulated media stories relevant to

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, I - I typically wouldn't be reading those stories. I mean, you're
getting so much information as a Minister, you can't - you're getting 100 and 150 emails a
day just to your APH account, let alone to your Human Services account.
MR GREGGERY: So the reliance, then, was primarily upon the media adviser -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Typically.
MR GREGGERY: - and staff.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: On your media - and your staff.
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: If there was significant stories which were breaking or developing
that they might bring to your attention.
MR GREGGERY: And in respect of at least that category of significant stories - and I'm talking
here about the Robodebt Scheme, to avoid being too general. When there was a great
degree of media scrutiny about the Scheme, was it your practice to be closely involved in the
detail of what the Department was releasing and what was coming from your office?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: No. I didn't always know what the Department was releasing,
because I knew that they - they were releasing some information, and they also had a public
spokesperson who was acting independently of me and, to my knowledge, of my office. And
he - he was very prominent in the media. Probably did a lot more media than I did.
MR GREGGERY: You're talking about Mr Jongen?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: What, then, do you say to the possibility of a process whereby the media
department of DHS would get information from the business area, draft a document, which
would be forwarded to your advisers, including your media adviser particularly, for review,
which would be forwarded to you for clearance and then back down the line for the
Department's media release?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: For the Department's media release? I don't - I don't recall a
Departmental media release coming up to me for review. If it's - I can't recall an instance of
that. I'm not saying it didn't happen, but I think it would be unusual if it did.
MR GREGGERY: In terms of your perception of the role of media while you were the
Minister, did you understand that the media can give a Minister a boost in terms of presence
generally, effectiveness, the appearance of doing a job well, but it can also be equally
detrimental to those qualities or the perception of those qualities?

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: The role of any political leader, in particular Minister, includes
working with the media to communicate what the government's message is. It's a very
important part of the role. It's an expected part of the role by the public and certainly by the
press corps.
MR GREGGERY: And you took that role seriously?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: I took every aspect of my role seriously.
COMMISSIONER: Mr Greggery, I think you might have got your media releases and articles
out of sync, because that article on the screen is the 3rd of March. It comes immediately
after the joint press release. But there's another one at tab 8 in my bundle at any rate, which
comes immediately after the 11th of March.
MR GREGGERY: That's quite right, Commissioner, yes. Sorry, Mr Tudge, I did get things out of
order. You will see the article on the screen, 'Cheats Cop Whack', was published 3 March
2016, which was the day after the joint media release with Mr Porter about the two bills to
be introduced to Parliament that day, the 2nd of March.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Right.
MR GREGGERY: I think I related that media release to the - related that article to the media
release at tab 7 -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: - that the welfare compliance measure was ahead of schedule, but you will
see that, in fact, the article at tab 8, 'Welfare Probe Claw Back 329 Million', Exhibit 4630,
follows the media release on 11 March 2016.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, it does. It's - I mean, I - I can't recall this. They're two different
stories which are quite - they're stories which are quite similar, one on the 3rd of March and
one on the 12th of March. Typically, if a paper has already broken the story, then another
paper wouldn't, unless they had new information. I can't see the new information there
contained in the 12th of March story. I will point out as well that obviously I have nothing to
do with the headlines, typically nor doesn't journalist that you're dealing with.
MR GREGGERY: No, I was just identifying the article as -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes, yes.
MR GREGGERY: - being the later one.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: They both appear to be, just from scanning them now, related to
that same information of the $329 million.

THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Certainly by a couple of months into your time as Minister, you sought
information from the Department about compliance and debt saving proposals which could
be introduced by you into future Budgets or legislation?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: There was two parts to that question. The first part yes. The second
part, no, that I couldn't technically introduce them, because it wasn't - it would have to be
introduced by the Social Services Minister.
MR GREGGERY: The ones I'm referring to are identified in part at tab 12, Exhibit 4632. It's an
Executive Minute -
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: - for your information, which was received by the Departmental Liaison
Officer in your office on 28 April 2016 and signed by you, 4 May 2016.
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And it's quite a detailed document, if you flick through it. I appreciate
substantial parts have been redacted for - to reflect various forms of privilege. But this was
the nature of information you were seeking from your Department in respect of savings
measures which accorded with the government's narrative of welfare integrity?
THE HON ALAN TUDGE: That's - that is correct.
